$doNotEditByHand: Re-run the extractor instead. A diff here after a version bump IS the drift report.
$format: JSON Lines. This first line is the header; each later line is one template case.

$sources.handWritten: 51 cases chosen for the parser hazard each one probes
$sources.corpus: 84 distinct template strings the reference compiler emitted across fixtures/corpus/, extracted mechanically by extract-templates.mjs

$fields.id: stable case name; corpus cases are prefixed `corpus:`
$fields.html: the template string as passed to _$template() (tags may be unclosed, attributes present)
$fields.closed: templateWithClosingTags: every tag closed, ALL attributes removed -- what upstream validates
$fields.ambiguous: true when the HTML parser is EXPECTED to restructure the markup
$fields.invalidMarkup: null when upstream's isInvalidMarkup() accepts it, else {html, browser}
$fields.tree: the tree parse5 builds from `html`, in body context
$fields.walk: every node with the firstChild/nextSibling expression that reaches it
$fields.markers: the walk entries that are dom-expressions comment markers
$fields.fromCorpus: true when the string was extracted from compiled corpus output rather than hand-written
$fields.sources: corpus cases only: every <family>/<preset>#<n> the identical string came from
$fields.flags: corpus cases only: the isImportNode/isSVG/isMathML arguments, null when the plugin omitted them

$howToUse: The emitter must produce the same firstChild/nextSibling path for a given template as the `walk` recorded here. Where invalidMarkup is non-null the template must be REJECTED at compile time, not walked.

script is raw text: the < inside is NOT a tag

textarea is ESCAPABLE raw text, unlike script which is raw text. A bare '<' in its content round-trips as '<', so upstream's validator rejects it while the otherwise-identical <script> case passes. Any '<' inside a textarea template must be pre-escaped by the emitter.
